_note: Sample Agent 3 output for H.R. 9041 (an opportunity bill) and the VoltRide demo company.

relevant_provisions.why: Bicycle parts imported for US assembly, including e-bikes, would enter duty-free for 10 years. VoltRide assembles in Oakland, so qualifying parts would get cheaper.
Employers could give tax-free reimbursements for buying an e-bike to commute, which should raise demand for commuter bikes.

not_relevant.reason: Road and infrastructure funding. Good for cycling overall, but no direct, measurable effect on VoltRide.

assumptions.statement: Duties make up about 8% of the landed cost of qualifying bicycle parts. PLACEHOLDER: replace with VoltRide's actual duties paid.
assumptions.source: None. company.json does not list duties separately.

assumptions.statement: Only frames, drivetrains, wheels, and small parts qualify. Batteries, motors, and controllers may not (check the tariff list in Sec. 8, note 34(f)).
Tax-free employer reimbursement raises VoltRide City sales about 3%
assumptions.source: None yet. Agent 2 should look for results from the earlier federal bike commuter benefit.

assumptions.statement: Setting up an employer sales program costs about $40,000
An employer program adds about 1% to City sales even without the tax benefit

options.name: Do nothing
options.description: Watch the bill. Act only if it moves.
